item.title: Hitsumabushi: Nagoya's Three-Way Eel Feast — Guide
item.description: Hitsumabushi is the flagship of ‘Nagoya meshi’, the city’s proudly idiosyncratic food culture, and it turns grilled eel into a ritual of three acts: finely sliced, crisp-grilled unagi arrives on rice in a lacquered wooden tub, and you eat the first quarter plain, the second with wasabi, spring onion and shredded nori, and the third drowned in hot dashi as a fragrant ochazuke — before finishing with a fourth portion in whichever style won.
